introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2021. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae booklets may be used.
incertitudes: Regles de choix : la consigne imprimee est « Section A obligatoire, puis DEUX questions de la Section B OU DEUX de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois ». Le systeme ne sait exprimer que « 2 parmi 3 » par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, pas de total par question. Le champ points de chaque exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions (Section A : 8 ou 9 ; Sections B et C : 17, ce qui est coherent avec « all questions carry equal marks »).

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) The rate of change of the radius of a circle is $2\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$ at the instant when the radius is $2\ \text{cm}$. Find the rate of change of the area of the circle. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$A=\pi r^2$, so by the chain rule $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{dA}{dr}\cdot\dfrac{dr}{dt}=2\pi r\,\dfrac{dr}{dt}$.

With $r=2$ and $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=2$: $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=2\pi(2)(2)=8\pi\approx25.1$.

**$\dfrac{dA}{dt}=8\pi\approx25.1\ \text{cm}^2\text{s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) Find the rate of change of the circumference of the circle. *[2 marks]*
(ii) The area bounded by the curve $y^2=x^2+1$, the $x$-axis and the ordinates $x=1$ and $x=3$ is rotated completely about the $x$-axis. Find the volume of the solid generated. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Volume of revolution about the $x$-axis: $V=\pi\displaystyle\int_a^b y^2\,dx$.

$$V=\pi\int_1^3(x^2+1)\,dx=\pi\left[\frac{x^3}{3}+x\right]_1^3.$$

At $x=3$: $\dfrac{27}{3}+3=12$. At $x=1$: $\dfrac13+1=\dfrac43$.

$V=\pi\left(12-\dfrac43\right)=\dfrac{32\pi}{3}\approx33.5$.

**$V=\dfrac{32\pi}{3}\approx33.5$ cubic units.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii) The position vectors of three particles of masses $2\,\text{kg}$, $5\,\text{kg}$ and $9\,\text{kg}$ are $(-2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})$, $(4\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j})$ and $(3\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j})$ respectively. Find the position vector of the centre of gravity of these three particles. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The centre of gravity $\bar{\mathbf r}$ is the weighted mean: $\bar{\mathbf r}=\dfrac{\sum m_i\mathbf r_i}{\sum m_i}$.

Total mass: $2+5+9=16$.

$\sum m_i\mathbf r_i=2(-2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)+5(4\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)+9(3\mathbf i+5\mathbf j)$

$=(-4+20+27)\mathbf i+(6-15+45)\mathbf j=43\mathbf i+36\mathbf j.$

$\bar{\mathbf r}=\dfrac{43\mathbf i+36\mathbf j}{16}=\dfrac{43}{16}\mathbf i+\dfrac94\mathbf j.$

**$\bar{\mathbf r}=\dfrac{43}{16}\mathbf i+\dfrac94\mathbf j\ (=2.6875\,\mathbf i+2.25\,\mathbf j)$.**
